title: Planaria lack morphological mutant lines; the only abnormal line is bioelectric

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria lack morphological mutant lines; the only abnormal line is bioelectric

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Unlike other model species, planaria have no reported morphologically abnormal genetic strains; the only abnormal line is a permanently two-headed form produced by manipulating bioelectric signalling rather than genes, which the authors say is predicted by their model for species like planaria.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In planaria this does not exist—no morphologically abnormal genetic strains have been reported. In fact, the only available abnormal line of planaria is a permanently two-headed form [96,97,98], which was produced not genetically but by manipulating bioelectrical signaling—the modality that is used to coordinate cellular competency [99,100,101], as is predicted by our model for species like planaria.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “4. Discussion › 4.4. The Paradox of Robustness: Why the Animal with the Worst Genome Has the Best Anatomy”. Scope: Planarian flatworms compared with other model organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The empirical catalog claim can be checked against public literature and resources, but incompleteness prevents strong confirmation of absence. The connection to the model remains an interpretation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Systematically search planarian stock centers, mutation screens, and literature for heritable morphological strains, and verify the induction and persistence mechanism of reported two-headed lines. One genetic morphological strain would refute the absolute absence claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The model prediction is not tested by cataloguing alone.

Absence of reports is difficult to establish exhaustively.

Morphological variants may be transient, environmental, or unpublished.

fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.36
discriminating power: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.52
data existence: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether abnormal genetic strains have been reported is a census of public records, and PlanMine plus the literature are the right places to look. The census does not cleanly separate stable mutants, clonal anomalies and transient knockdowns, and it cannot show that the model predicted the two-headed line rather than accommodating it. The empirical half is only partly decidable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Search PlanMine phenotype records and the planarian literature for stable, heritable, morphologically abnormal strains, and separate them from RNAi knockdowns and from the bioelectrically induced two-headed line. A heritable morphological mutant line would refute the universal negative; finding only the two-headed bioelectric line would support it under a strict definition of genetic strain.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
RNAi morphological phenotypes are easily counted as genetic strains.

The negative claim is definition- and date-sensitive, and sexual-strain genetics are sparsely reported.

fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.48
